name: Pride (superbia) as capital vice
plainSummary: In the classic list, pride is the disordered elevation of self—elevating the self above God, truth, or the good of others.
description: Derived principle from Christian moral tradition: pride (superbia) is a root distortion of self-love—excessive esteem for oneself, contempt for dependence on God or others—often treated as ordering or amplifying other vices.
foundationStrengthRationale: Stable as a category within centuries of Christian theology and spiritual literature; secular or interfaith readers may reject the metaphysical framing while recognizing hubris as a moral phenomenon.

pros.claim: Names a recurring moral failure—hubris—that appears across cultures and institutions.
pros.evidence: Philosophy and literature independently criticize arrogance, self-deception, and contempt for limits; the tradition gives these a structured place.

cons.claim: Can be misread to condemn healthy self-respect or legitimate ambition.
cons.evidence: Pastoral and feminist critiques warn that pride language has sometimes been used to suppress dignity and assertiveness among the oppressed.
